title: Saving Energy with Per-Variable Bitwidth Speculation
problem: Compilers for tiny embedded devices directly translate source-level variable bitwidths (e.g., 32-bit integers) to binary without exploiting the fact that most variables use far fewer bits than declared at runtime. This wastes energy in computations and memory traffic on highly optimized, energy-constrained devices where further traditional optimizations are difficult.
motivation: Tiny IoT devices operate under tight energy budgets but cannot afford to sacrifice performance, and their hardware is already heavily optimized, making bitwidth reduction a rare remaining source of energy savings.
method: BitSpec is a compiler-architecture co-design: the compiler statically narrows variable bitwidths to their predicted (expected) needs and emits speculative narrow-bitwidth instructions. The hardware monitors live values in speculative variables; when a value overflows the narrowed representation, hardware reports a misspeculation event to software, which re-executes the affected computation at the original (safe) bitwidth. This speculation-recovery loop ensures correctness while capturing energy savings during the common case where narrow widths suffice.
key_novelty: Fine-grained per-variable bitwidth speculation with hardware misspeculation detection, allowing transparent compiler-driven bitwidth reduction without requiring programmer annotation or profile-guided static analysis.
contributions: BitSpec: a compiler pass that speculatively narrows per-variable bitwidths to their expected runtime needs.
A lightweight hardware monitor that detects bitwidth misspeculation (overflow) and triggers software re-execution at full bitwidth.
Energy reduction of 9.9% on average and up to 28.2% on tiny-device workloads, with correctness guaranteed by the speculation-recovery mechanism.
limitations: The overhead of misspeculation recovery and the cost of the hardware monitor on area and timing are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Speculative per-variable bitwidth narrowing for energy savings on embedded devices
